label: Strictly better prevention: a supplied comparison of preventing with permitting an event
definition: PreventionWays.Better b e: preventing e is strictly better overall than permitting it. A supplied primitive: no axiology, aggregation rule or link to Rowe's costs is built in. Because it is free, arguments through it relocate rather than derive Rowe's constraint.
note: Analyst formulation for the trolley pilot (owner direction 2026-11-28), attribution deferred. See docs/notes/trolley-principles.md.

formal_gap.meaning: Whether preventing the event e is strictly better, all things considered, than permitting it, for the preventer b; a supplied comparison over the Rowe signature.
examples: Preventing a fawn's intense suffering at no cost to any good would be strictly better than permitting it.
exclusions: A mere difference in lives saved without an overall comparison.
Rowe's blocking cost itself: the link between the two is the open outcome bridge.
open_obligations: The axiology and aggregation rule (whether several lesser costs can jointly outweigh a suffering) are unspecified.
No relation to Rowe's Cost, GreaterGood or EqualOrWorseEvil fields is assumed; the outcome bridge supplies one direction as an open premise.
